headline: First Hispanic U.S. senator
summary: Louisiana's legislature elected Bouligny to the Senate in 1824.
qualifier: The Senate Historical Office revised this attribution in October 2026; older references name Octaviano Larrazolo. Bouligny was born a Spanish citizen in Spanish-ruled New Orleans. When Spanish loyalists were encouraged to relocate after the Louisiana Purchase, Bouligny resigned from the Spanish military and remained in New Orleans.

headline: First black member to serve in the U.S. House
summary: Rainey began House service in December 1870.
qualifier: Date denotes House service, not Election Day. Revels had already entered the Senate.

headline: First black member of Congress
summary: Revels took his Senate oath on February 25, 1870.
qualifier: Revels was elected to complete an existing term ending in March 1871. Opponents challenged his eligibility, citing the Dred Scott decision and the Senate’s nine-year citizenship requirement.

headline: First Hispanic voting representative elected to the U.S. House
summary: Pacheco's initial 1876 victory sent him to the House in 1877.
qualifier: This concerns a voting representative; territorial delegates had served earlier. The House later resolved his contested election against him in 1878; he won again in 1879.

headline: First black senator to complete a full term
summary: Bruce completed his six-year Senate term in 1881, after election by the Mississippi legislature in 1874.
qualifier: Election: February 4, 1874. Service: March 4, 1875–March 3, 1881. The timeline year is completion, not election. He was the second black senator, after Hiram Revels.

headline: First Jewish U.S. Supreme Court justice
summary: Brandeis joined the Court in 1916.
qualifier: Supreme Court justices are appointed and confirmed, not elected.

headline: First woman elected to Congress
summary: Following her election, reporters focused on the important issues, asking about her clothes, her recipes, and the color of her hair.
qualifier: Election year and service year differ. House firsts records her oath/service on April 2, 1917.

headline: First woman to serve in the U.S. Senate
summary: Though she was a journalist, feminist, and suffragist, Felton was also a white supremacist.
qualifier: Appointed October 3; sworn in November 21 and replaced November 22. She was not elected.

headline: First woman to serve as a U.S. state governor
summary: Ross became Wyoming's governor in 1925 after winning an election to replace her late husband.
qualifier: Miriam Ferguson also won a governorship in 1924 but took office later in January 1925; this record is the service first.

headline: First Native American elected vice president
summary: Though a citizen of the Kaw Nation, Curtis supported policies that undermined tribal sovereignty.
qualifier: Curtis won the vice presidency with Herbert Hoover in 1928.

headline: First woman elected to the U.S. Senate
summary: Known as "Silent Hattie" for only speaking 15 times on the Senate floor, Caraway won a special election in January 1932.
qualifier: She had already entered the Senate by appointment in November 1931; her service therefore predates her election.

headline: First Asian American voting member elected to Congress
summary: When he first settled in the United States, federal law prevented Indians from becoming citizens.
qualifier: The voting-member qualification distinguishes him from earlier Asian territorial delegates and resident commissioners.

headline: First Asian American U.S. senator
summary: Fong entered the Senate when Hawaii became a state in 1959.
qualifier: Hawaii's formal statehood and senators' term start were August 21; the oath followed on August 24.

headline: First woman of color elected to Congress
summary: The third-generation Japanese American served a total of 12 terms in Congress.
qualifier: She was also the first Asian American woman in Congress.

headline: First black senator elected by popular vote
summary: Brooke won election in 1966 and entered the Senate in 1967, ending a nearly 86-year absence of black senators.
qualifier: Revels and Bruce had been selected by state legislatures. The 86-year interval runs from Bruce leaving in 1881 to Brooke serving in 1967.

headline: First black U.S. Supreme Court justice
summary: Marshall joined the Court in 1967.
qualifier: Supreme Court justices are appointed and confirmed, not elected.

headline: First black woman elected to Congress
summary: Chisholm bucked traditional expectations of freshmen representatives to not "rock the boat," becoming an immediately vocal advocate on issues such as the Vietnam War.
qualifier: Chisholm’s freshman class included two other black members, increasing black representation in the U.S. House from six to nine.

headline: First woman elected governor without following a husband in that office
summary: Grasso also won Connecticut's governorship again in 1978, but would resign two years later after a cancer diagnosis.
qualifier: Often phrased “in her own right,” the distinction is that her husband had not been governor. Earlier women governors had been elected.

headline: First woman U.S. Supreme Court justice
summary: O’Connor joined the Court in 1981.
qualifier: Supreme Court justices are appointed and confirmed, not elected.

headline: First woman principal chief of the Cherokee Nation
summary: Mankiller became principal chief in 1985 and won election in 1987.
qualifier: This is a sovereign tribal nation, not a U.S. state. She first succeeded a departing chief, then won her own elections.

headline: First Hispanic woman elected to Congress
summary: Ros-Lehtinen fled Cuba with her family at 8 years old, after Castro had taken power.
qualifier: House service began August 29, 1989.

headline: First black governor elected by voters
summary: Wilder had previously won a special election to the Virginia state Senate in 1969.
qualifier: P. B. S. Pinchback had served as Louisiana governor through succession in 1872. Wilder's distinction is popular election.

headline: First black woman elected to the U.S. Senate
summary: Moseley Braun would later become ambassador to New Zealand and vie for the Democratic presidential nomination.
qualifier: She was also Illinois's first woman senator.

headline: First Puerto Rican woman elected to Congress
summary: Velázquez later became the first Hispanic woman to serve as ranking member of a full House committee.
qualifier: Representing a New York district — not to be confused with an election to Puerto Rico's resident commissioner position.

headline: First openly gay challenger elected to Congress
summary: Baldwin won her first House election in 1998 while openly gay. She was also the first openly lesbian candidate elected to the Wisconsin State Assembly.
qualifier: Earlier members came out while already in Congress. Baldwin was openly gay when she first won a seat.

headline: First Jewish vice-presidential nominee on a major-party ticket
summary: Connecticut Senator Joe Lieberman was Al Gore’s running mate in 2000.
qualifier: Gore and Lieberman lost the election; Lieberman did not serve as vice president.

headline: First Muslim elected to Congress
summary: Ellison won Minnesota's Fifth District seat in 2006.
qualifier: Religious identification is publicly documented by the Minnesota Legislative Reference Library.

headline: First black president elected
summary: Obama won the 2008 presidential election and was inaugurated January 20, 2009.
qualifier: Obama was re-elected in 2012, defeating Mitt Romney.

headline: First openly gay man elected to Congress as a non-incumbent
summary: Polis won Colorado’s 2nd Congressional District in 2008.
qualifier: Earlier gay men had served in Congress; this first concerns a man who was openly gay when initially elected.

headline: First Hispanic U.S. Supreme Court justice
summary: Sotomayor joined the Court in 2009.
qualifier: Supreme Court justices are appointed and confirmed, not elected.

headline: First Asian American woman governor elected
summary: As governor, Haley appointed Tim Scott to a vacant U.S. Senate seat, making him South Carolina’s first black senator.
qualifier: Also the state's first woman governor; elected in the same cycle as Susana Martinez (R-NM).

headline: First Latina governor elected
summary: In 2017, Martinez vetoed legislation that would have increased New Mexico’s minimum wage.
qualifier: She and Nikki Haley were the first women of color elected to U.S. state governorships in the same election cycle.

headline: First openly gay parent serving in Congress
summary: Polis and his partner became parents while he was serving in the House.
qualifier: This milestone occurred in 2011, three years after his first congressional election.

headline: First openly gay U.S. senator elected
summary: Baldwin won her Senate election in 2012.
qualifier: Also Wisconsin’s first woman senator. This milestone concerns being openly gay at the time of election.

headline: First disabled woman veteran elected to the U.S. House
summary: Duckworth was born in Thailand and raised in Hawaii. She lost her right leg near the hip and her left leg below the knee while deployed in Iraq.
qualifier: The Smithsonian oral-history collection identifies her as the first disabled woman veteran elected to each chamber.

headline: First Hindu elected to Congress
summary: Gabbard has described growing up studying both the Bhagavad Gita and the New Testament.
qualifier: Pew's research relied on congressional questionnaires, follow-up interviews and supplementary research.

headline: First Asian American woman and first Buddhist elected to the Senate
summary: Hirono's 2012 Senate election established two representation firsts.
qualifier: Religious affiliation is documented in Pew's original congressional research; Senate history documents the gender and ancestry milestone.

headline: First Latina elected to the U.S. Senate
summary: Cortez Masto had previously served as Nevada's attorney general and succeeded Sen. Harry Reid on his retirement.
qualifier: She entered the Senate in 2017 and was also Nevada's first woman senator.

headline: First openly transgender person elected to a state legislature and subsequently seated
summary: Roem was a journalist for more than a decade before running for the Virginia House of Delegates seat.
qualifier: In 1992, Althea Garrison was elected in Massachusetts and was outed after the election. Stacie Laughton was elected in New Hampshire in 2012 while openly transgender but did not take that seat. Roem was both elected while openly transgender and seated.

headline: First U.S. senator to give birth while in office
summary: Duckworth had previously introduced the Friendly Airports for Mothers (FAM) Act, which required airports to provide safe, clean, and accessible lactation areas for mothers.
qualifier: Her official biography also records a subsequent Senate rule change allowing infants on the floor.

headline: First Muslim women elected to Congress
summary: Omar, elected in Minnesota, is Somali-American and a refugee, and Tlaib, elected in Michigan, is Palestinian-American.
qualifier: A shared first, distinct from Keith Ellison's 2006 election as the first Muslim member.

headline: First Native American women elected to Congress
summary: Davids, a member of the Ho-Chunk Nation, is the first openly LGBTQ Native American elected to Congress and the first openly LGBTQ person elected to Congress from Kansas. Haaland, of the Laguna Pueblo tribe, later served as U.S. Secretary of the Interior in the Biden cabinet.
qualifier: A shared first: Davids represented Kansas and Haaland New Mexico.

headline: First openly gay man elected governor
summary: Polis also became Colorado’s first Jewish governor. In 2021 he became the first sitting U.S. governor to marry a same-sex partner.
qualifier: Oregon’s bisexual governor Kate Brown had already won election in 2016. Polis was the first openly gay man elected governor.

headline: First woman, black American and South Asian American elected vice president
dimensions: Women; black; Asian American; South Asian
summary: Harris's father is Afro-Jamaican and her mother is Indian.
qualifier: The 2020 election and Harris’s January 2021 inauguration are separate milestones.

headline: First openly gay Afro-Latino elected to Congress
summary: Torres and Mondaire Jones were elected in the same 2020 election, becoming the first openly gay black men elected to Congress.
qualifier: An intersectional milestone; his own floor remarks identify him as the first LGBTQ Afro-Latino member.

headline: First openly lesbian governors elected
summary: Healey (Massachusetts) and Kotek (Oregon) won governorships in the same 2022 election.
qualifier: Shared election first.

headline: First Alaska Native elected to Congress
summary: Peltola won Alaska’s 2022 House special election. She ran for the U.S. Senate in 2026; the race was still being counted at the research cutoff.
qualifier: She was also the first woman and first Alaska-born person elected to the U.S. House from Alaska, and the first Democrat to hold the seat since 1972.

headline: First Korean American elected to the U.S. Senate
summary: Kim is also the first Asian-American to represent New Jersey in the Senate.
qualifier: After winning election, he was appointed to the remainder of the preceding term and took office in December 2024.

headline: First openly transgender person elected to Congress
summary: McBride was also the first openly transgender person elected as a state senator in the United States.
qualifier: The congressional service milestone occurred in 2025; her earlier state Senate election was in 2020.

headline: Two black women serve in the U.S. Senate together for the first time
person: Angela Alsobrooks and Lisa Blunt Rochester
summary: Alsobrooks and Blunt Rochester began their Senate terms together in January 2025.
qualifier: Each also became the first black senator elected from her state; Blunt Rochester was Delaware’s first woman senator.

headline: New York City’s first Muslim mayor takes office
summary: Zohran Mamdani took office as New York City’s first Muslim mayor.
qualifier: Municipal scope: New York City, not all of New York state.

headline: Detroit’s first woman mayor takes office
summary: Mary Sheffield took office as Detroit’s first woman mayor.
qualifier: A municipal milestone: Detroit had not previously had a woman mayor.

headline: Nevada elects its first black governor
summary: Nevada’s attorney general defeated the Republican incumbent, Joe Lombardo.
qualifier: First-black milestone source is a partisan organization; transition confirms win, certification not found.

headline: Ohio elects its first woman governor
summary: The first woman elected governor of Ohio had previously served as the state's Director of Health.
qualifier: Nancy Hollister previously served via succession, 1998–1999. Incoming; certification unverified.

headline: Rhode Island elects its first openly LGBTQ+ statewide official
summary: The first openly LGBTQ+ statewide election winner in Rhode Island is a former prosecutor and chaired the state's cannabis commission.
qualifier: Incoming officeholder; certification not independently verified. Service year is prospective.

headline: South Carolina elects its first woman senator
summary: The first woman elected U.S. senator from South Carolina is also the first Democrat to win a Senate election in the state since 1998.
qualifier: Darline Graham preceded her by appointment in July 2026. Andrews is the first woman elected to this seat, not the first woman to serve from the state.

headline: Tennessee elects its first woman governor
summary: Blackburn had served as a Senator for Tennessee since 2019, and before that in Congress since 2003.
qualifier: Incoming officeholder; certification not independently verified. Service year is prospective.

headline: A black woman wins a U.S. governorship
summary: The former mayor of Atlanta also becomes Georgia's first female governor.
qualifier: Incoming officeholder; service year is prospective.

headline: Mississippi elects a black senator for the first time since 1874
summary: Colom’s reported win makes him the first black Mississippian elected to the U.S. Senate since Blanche K. Bruce in 1874.
qualifier: Bruce was elected by the state legislature in 1874 and last served in 1881. Colom’s Senate service is expected to begin in 2027.

headline: Wisconsin elects its first black governor
summary: At 40, Crowley is expected to become the youngest sitting U.S. governor when he takes office in 2027.
qualifier: Official transition site confirms election; first-black milestone supported by LDF. Incoming in 2027.

headline: South Carolina appoints its first woman senator
summary: Darline Graham was appointed following the death of her brother, Lindsey Graham.
qualifier: Appointed rather than elected. Annie Andrews subsequently won the November 2026 election. Date is appointment announcement.

headline: Florida elects its first black governor
summary: The Republican previously served in the Florida state House and in Congress.
qualifier: Certification scheduled November 17; incoming in 2027.

headline: A Muslim is elected to the U.S. Senate
summary: The Egyptian-American's father had been an imam.
qualifier: Incoming officeholder; service year is prospective.

headline: Texas elects its first openly LGBTQ+ statewide official
summary: The first openly LGBTQ+ person elected statewide in Texas is also the state's first woman elected chief justice.
qualifier: This is an elected judicial office, separate from legislative representation.

headline: A Native American woman is elected to the Senate
summary: The Ojibwe activist had served as lieutenant governor under Tim Walz.
qualifier: Earlier Native American men served in the Senate. Flanagan is the first Native American woman elected.

headline: A Native American woman wins a U.S. governorship
summary: With Stephanie Garcia Richard as running mate, they are the first all woman-of-color ticket for governor and lieutenant governor to be elected in the U.S. See Haaland's other firsts elsewhere in the timeline.
qualifier: Incoming officeholder; service year is prospective.

headline: New Jersey elects its first Muslim member of Congress
summary: First Muslim elected to Congress from New Jersey. U.S. senator Tammy Duckworth credits Hamawy with saving her life when they were both serving in the Iraq War in 2004, where Hamawy was a U.S. Army physician.
qualifier: Incoming officeholder; service year is prospective.

headline: Texas elects its first Latina governor
summary: Hinojosa is also the first Democrat to be elected governor of Texas since Ann Richards in 1990.
qualifier: Incoming officeholder; service year is prospective.

headline: Indiana elects its first openly LGBTQ+ member of Congress
summary: Ford had served in the Indiana state Senate before his election to Congress.
qualifier: Incoming officeholder; service year is prospective.

headline: Colorado elects its first black woman to Congress
summary: Kiros is the first Gen Z woman elected to Congress. She defeated a 15-term incumbent in the Democratic primary.
qualifier: Incoming officeholder; service year is prospective.

headline: Minnesota elects its first woman governor
summary: Klobuchar had been Minnesota's first female Senator when elected in 2006.
qualifier: Incoming officeholder; service year is prospective.

headline: Louisiana elects its first Republican woman senator
summary: Letlow had served in the U.S. House since 2021. She and John Fleming advanced past incumbent Bill Cassidy in the Republican primary; Letlow won their runoff before the November election.
qualifier: Party-specific first; Louisiana previously elected Democratic women to the Senate.

headline: Michigan elects its first openly LGBTQ+ member of Congress
summary: First openly LGBTQ+ person elected to Congress from Michigan.
qualifier: Incoming officeholder; service year is prospective.

headline: An openly gay man is elected to the U.S. Senate
summary: Pappas is also the first openly gay man to represent New Hampshire in Congress.
qualifier: Openly lesbian and bisexual senators preceded him. This first concerns an openly gay man.

headline: Nebraska elects its first Latina to Congress
summary: The first Latina elected to Congress from Nebraska is also the first Democratic woman elected to the House from this state.
qualifier: Incoming officeholder; service year is prospective.

headline: Election sets up three black women serving in the Senate
summary: Stratton’s election sets up a record three black women serving together in the U.S. Senate in 2027.
qualifier: Prospective 2027 record alongside Angela Alsobrooks and Lisa Blunt Rochester; not Illinois's first black woman senator.

headline: New York elects its first Native American woman to Congress
summary: In 2025, Valdez was arrested at a protest at the New York offices of U.S. senators Chuck Schumer and Kirsten Gillibrand calling for an end to U.S. weapons sales to Israel.
qualifier: Incoming officeholder; service year is prospective.

headline: Michigan elects its first openly transgender woman legislator
summary: The first openly transgender woman elected to Michigan's legislature was a megachurch pastor and podcaster who had undergone Christian conversion therapy for 15 years.
qualifier: State of Michigan first, not a national first.

headline: 18 states have never had a black U.S. representative
summary: The House historian’s state-by-state roster identifies 18 states without a black member of Congress.
qualifier: See the map for the states and distinctions between election and service.

headline: 41 states have never had a black U.S. senator
summary: Nine states have been represented by black senators, including senators who were appointed.
qualifier: See the map for the states and distinctions between election and service.

headline: At least 29 states have neither had nor elected a Hispanic U.S. representative
summary: Eighteen states have had Hispanic House members. Nebraska and North Carolina elected their first in 2026; service begins in 2027. New Hampshire requires further review.
qualifier: New Hampshire is unverified: congressional historical rosters do not list John E. Sununu, whose father, governor John H. Sununu, publicly identified as partly Hispanic. A parent’s identity does not establish how the son identifies.

headline: At least 38 states have not had a Hispanic U.S. senator
summary: The Senate Historical Office lists Hispanic senators from eleven states. New Hampshire requires further review.
qualifier: New Hampshire is unverified: congressional historical rosters do not list John E. Sununu, whose father, governor John H. Sununu, publicly identified as partly Hispanic. A parent’s identity does not establish how the son identifies.

headline: Mississippi has never sent a woman to the U.S. House
summary: It is the only state still without this first.
qualifier: CAWP reported that no women filed for Mississippi’s U.S. House races in 2026. Cindy Hyde-Smith has served in the Senate; this claim concerns the House only.

headline: 49 states have neither had nor elected a Muslim U.S. senator
summary: Michigan elected the first Muslim senator in 2026; he has not yet taken office.
qualifier: See the map for the states and distinctions between election and service.

headline: 14 states have neither had nor elected a woman governor
summary: Fourteen states remain without a woman governor after accounting for the 2026 election winners; three additional states elected their first women governors, who have not yet taken office.
qualifier: See the map for the states and distinctions between election and service.

headline: 15 states have never had a woman U.S. senator
summary: Fifteen states have never been represented by a woman in the Senate, including appointed senators.
qualifier: See the map for the states and distinctions between election and service.
